title: Make hand-written job records detectable by the gate (§16.2)
summary: Retry of job 20261010-162440-2gwj (dropped, never verified; its refusal came from naming the nonexistent crates/athena-gate/tests/history.rs, so no earlier finding is carried over). Extend the gate in crates/athena-gate so the three §16.2 fabrications (a whole job by hand, a forged landing of a dispatched-but-never-closed job, a hand-made proposal closed with `athena close`) are refused or flagged. Tests go in the existing src/landing_tests.rs, not a new tests/ file. Audience: the owner running the gate and CI.

defaults_applied.how: All changes are Rust in crates/athena-gate.
Criteria require cargo test, clippy and fmt clean.
The rule is enforced in the gate, not by prose.
Tests build each forgery and assert a Violation.
All three §16.2 paths are covered, not the one that surfaced.
Docs state detected cases and residual plainly.
Verifier runs cargo test on forged histories.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Code survey: read crates/athena-gate/src/jobs.rs (check() runs per added records/jobs/ file via AnyRecord::parse; Score re-computed by expected_score, Outcome Landed handling follows at line ~349), crates/athena-gate/src/history.rs (check_history, check_after_cutover), and crates/athena-gate/src/landing_tests.rs (helpers stage_landing, judge, history_of, opening, closing; tests like a_squash_with_a_forged_rescore_is_still_refused). Entry point is the gate's per-commit check calling jobs::check, then history::check_history over the range; records validation goes through AnyRecord::parse and canonical_path, with check_record_file and the AnyRecord round-trip test in athena-data covering any new record field. The property is measured directly by building forged histories in landing_tests.rs and asserting the Violation list.

Job 20261010-162440-2gwj is addressed as follows: its only recorded outcome was refusal for naming crates/athena-gate/tests/history.rs, which does not exist; this reading uses only existing files. Its candidate changed no files, so its listed scope (jobs.rs, landing_tests.rs, history.rs, athena-v0.md, enforcement.md, CHANGELOG.md) is kept and widened to all three forgeries; its out_of_scope narrowing to one forgery is dropped.

Detection relies on in-repo evidence Athena always writes for a real run (opening records committed before the work, invocation/dispatch records, proposal provenance for a closed proposal) and refuses records that lack it or contradict their ordering; a deliberate forger who mimics all of it still passes, and the docs say so.
The newly refused share of past readings is small since real jobs carry this evidence: expected 5% of newly refused readings.
Design/docs update: §16.2 of docs/design/athena-v0.md and docs/enforcement.md are rewritten to say which forgeries are now detected and what residual remains.
question: Without signing, any in-repo evidence can be forged by someone who copies Athena's format. Is detection of inconsistency (missing run-time evidence such as invocation and dispatch records ordered before the work) enough, with keyed MACs or an outside ledger still out of scope?

acceptance_criteria.text: Run `cargo test -p athena-gate`: new tests in crates/athena-gate/src/landing_tests.rs build (a) a job whose records were all written by hand across two commits, (b) a single forged commit landing a job that was dispatched but never closed, and (c) a hand-made proposal closed with athena close; each yields at least one Violation, and the existing genuine-landing tests still pass.
Run `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check`: both clean; `cargo test --workspace` passes.

The change refuses more readings than before and the higher refusal rate is intended: expected 5% of newly refused readings against the repository's own genuine job history; `cargo test -p athena-gate` includes a test that the repository's real history shape (a genuine landing) is not refused.
Each refusal Violation's detail and repair text names the missing or contradicting evidence, so the owner can tell what to fix; checkable by Grep in crates/athena-gate/src/jobs.rs and history.rs.

docs/design/athena-v0.md §16.2 and docs/enforcement.md no longer say the three forgeries pass; they state what is detected and the residual (consistent, fully mimicked records still pass without signing).
CHANGELOG.md has an entry describing the new detection.

Any new record field is accepted by the records allow-list: Grep shows check_record_file / the AnyRecord round-trip test covering it, and the change does not touch athena.toml, defaults.toml, workflows or prompt files.

out_of_scope: Keyed MAC, signing, or a witness ledger outside the repo
Changes to athena.toml, defaults.toml, workflows, setup.sh or prompt files
Making a perfectly mimicked forgery undetectable-proof
departures: Three distinct forgeries in a gate with no signing make this broader and harder than the reference jobs, so cost, time and pass rate are worse.
urgent_reason: Re-queued request: the earlier reading was refused on every batch and wasted a job slot each time, so a correct file list cuts that repeated planning-stop waste.
hard_reason: Adds rules to the gate that can refuse landings and changes the history check, so a mistake wrongly blocks work or leaves forgery undetected.
